learning_outcomes.text: Master the basics of chemistry, especially the general relationships in the periodic table.
Ability to abstractly formulate chemical facts.
Master chemical calculations and the basics of matter structure.
Acquire the ability to argue linguistically and logically correctly and to communicate scientific facts understandably (judgment/evaluation).
Students will develop a fundamental understanding of chemical methods and will be able to solve inorganic chemistry calculation problems independently.
Experimental work in a chemical laboratory.
Perform and evaluate chemical laboratory experiments.
Critical analysis of experimental results, including report generation.
Teamwork through working in small groups (communication, problem-solving).

syllabus_topics: Self-organization, critical questioning and reporting, interdisciplinary thinking, presentation of exercise tasks.
assessment_rules: The prerequisite for receiving credit points is a passed written examination. Successful participation in the practical work is a prerequisite for taking the examination. The importance of the grade for the final grade is determined in the Bachelor's examination regulations.
